Effects:

If you succeed, deal elemental damage equal to your ranks in Resolve to every creature and doll within 1 range band, including allies.

remoulding.name: Energy Overflow
remoulding.flavor: Controlled output means the wave goes out, not back in. A shaped emission doesn't care about range; it cares about who it's aimed at.

If you succeed, deal elemental damage equal to your ranks in Resolve to every enemy within 2 range bands.
opportunities: (op)(op): Each enemy hit also suffers the Burning condition.

remoulding.name: Total Saturation
remoulding.flavor: At full output, collapse energy doesn't just burn. It tears. Whatever survives the initial wave is still bleeding, disoriented, and on fire.
remoulding.activation:

Effects:

If you succeed, deal elemental damage equal to your ranks in Resolve to every enemy within 3 range bands. Each enemy hit also suffers the Burning condition.

If you succeed, deal elemental damage equal to your ranks in Resolve to every enemy within 3 range bands. Each enemy hit also suffers the Burning condition.
opportunities: (op)(op): Each enemy hit also suffers the Bleeding and Dazed conditions.

remoulding.name: Elemental Aegis
remoulding.flavor: Collapse energy can be turned inward as easily as it's directed out. The practical result is a sustained field that makes you considerably harder to put down.
remoulding.activation:

Effects:

If you succeed, you gain the Resilient and Hardened conditions.

remoulding.name: Projected Aegis
remoulding.flavor: Extending the field to someone else means giving up your own coverage. You take the risk. They take the protection. That's the trade.

If you succeed, your target gains the Resilient and Hardened conditions.

remoulding.name: Iron Sky
remoulding.flavor: A full-coverage field costs everything the unit has. The squad walks through whatever comes next wearing that cost.

If you succeed, you and each target ally gain the Resilient and Hardened conditions.

remoulding.name: Battlefield Logistics
remoulding.flavor: A burst of collapse energy applied to your own frame gets you where you need to be. Tactical repositioning stops being an action tax when the energy is free.

remoulding.name: Tactical Relay
remoulding.flavor: Getting your team into position matters more than getting there yourself. A well-placed ally is worth two who are stuck in the wrong spot.

remoulding.name: Forced Displacement
remoulding.flavor: The collapse burst doesn't care whether the target wants to move. Sending an enemy into a worse position is logistics applied to the other side of the board, and the landing hurts.

remoulding.name: Terraforming
remoulding.flavor: A shockwave of collapse energy doesn't just damage what it touches. It changes it. An open path becomes a hazard in under a second, and the enemy spends the rest of the fight working around it.

remoulding.name: Denial Zone
remoulding.flavor: Entanglement slows people down. Dangerous ground and radiation keep them out entirely. When you need to hold a position rather than just slow someone through it, the distinction matters.

remoulding.name: Total Terrain Dominance
remoulding.flavor: At full output, the environment stops being a backdrop and starts being a piece you control. Raised ground, blinded sight lines, denied zones: the battlefield becomes whatever you need it to be.

science.name: Ballistic Analysis
science.flavor: Every bullet tells a story. The angle of impact, the depth of penetration, the pattern of spatter, all of these reveal information about the weapon that fired the shot and the position of the shooter. A trained eye can reconstruct the events of a firefight from nothing but the aftermath.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

Make a TN 2 Science (Precision) check to analyze ballistic evidence such as wounds, bullet impacts, or blast patterns.

Effects:

On a success, you determine the approximate location of the attack's origin point.
opportunities: Precision (op): Determine additional details about the weapon used, including its Damage and Deadliness.

science.name: Chemical Analysis
science.flavor: The modern battlefield is awash in chemical compounds, from industrial pollutants to military-grade toxins. Understanding what a substance is, where it came from, and how to counter it can mean the difference between life and death in contaminated environments.

science.name: Activation:

Make a TN 2 Science (Resilience) check to analyze a chemical sample (liquid, powder, aerosol, or residue).

Effects:

On a success, you identify its composition and typical properties, and infer likely origin sources or manufacturing methods.
opportunities: Resilience (op): Determine a method to synthesize or neutralize the substance.

science.name: Combat Stimulant
science.flavor: Stimulants borrow capability from the future. A medic who understands the pharmacology knows how much to borrow and when to stop.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Medicine (Power) check targeting one willing character at range 0 (including yourself).

Effects:

On a success, until the end of the scene, once per round the target may reduce the TN of one check by 1 before rolling. Each time they activate this benefit, they gain 2 strife.
opportunities: Power (op): The target also removes 3 fatigue immediately.
Power (op)(op): The TN reduction is 2 instead of 1 each time the target activates this benefit.

science.name: Device Modification
science.flavor: A piece of equipment rarely does exactly what you need it to do in exactly the situation you find yourself in. An engineer who can close that gap is worth more than the equipment itself.

Effects:

On a success, add or remove one item quality from the target item. The modification lasts until the end of the scene or until deliberately reversed. The GM has final say on which qualities may be added based on the item's nature and available materials.
opportunities: Precision (op): The modification is permanent until deliberately reversed.
Precision (op)(op): Add or remove a second quality from the same item.

science.name: Emergency Aid
science.flavor: Thirty seconds of focused attention and the right supplies can buy a casualty an hour. The medic who can provide both while taking fire earns a debt that cannot be repaid.

opportunities: Swiftness (op): Remove one additional eligible condition from the target.

science.name: Emergency Frame Stabilization
science.flavor: A T-Doll in the field does not have the luxury of a proper repair bay. A technician who can stabilize the most critical damage with what is in the kit is the next best option.

science.name: Activation:

Effects:

On a success, remove one condition of your choice (Bleeding, Dazed, or Disoriented) from the target.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): Remove one additional eligible condition from the target.
Swiftness (op)(op): The target also removes 2 fatigue.

science.name: Emergency Patch
science.flavor: Getting a piece of gear functional right now matters more than getting it fixed correctly later. A rough patch that holds through the engagement buys time to do the job properly.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:

Effects:

On a success, the target item removes the Damaged quality and becomes functional.
opportunities: Swiftness (op)(op): The repair holds through the next instance of damage the item would normally receive; the item does not gain the Damaged quality from that instance.

science.name: Emergency Triage
science.flavor: In the aftermath of violence, seconds matter. A trained medic can assess multiple casualties in moments, identifying who needs immediate attention and who can wait. This rapid categorization saves lives when resources are limited and time is short.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Medicine (Swiftness) check to assess all characters within range 0-1.

Effects:

On a success, you identify which characters are injured and the general severity of their wounds, ordered from most critical to least.
opportunities: Swiftness (op)+: Identify one specific injury per (op) spent this way, in order from most life-threatening to least.

science.name: Examine for ELID
science.flavor: The signs of Collapse infection are distinctive to those who know what to look for. Discoloration of the skin, the texture of emerging crystalline growths, the pattern of silicification. A trained observer can determine how far the disease has progressed without exposing themselves to the radiation the infected emit.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation: Activation: Make a TN 2 Science (Precision) check to visually assess a creature or body for signs of ELID infection. Effects: On a success, you determine whether the subject is infected and, if so, the current stage of ELID progression (Early, Middle, or Late).

science.name: Field Dressing
science.flavor: The fundamentals of wound care do not change on a battlefield. What changes is the environment in which you apply them.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Medicine (Precision) check targeting one character at range 0.

Effects:

On a success, the target removes fatigue equal to 3 plus your bonus successes.
opportunities: Precision (op): The next Medicine check targeting this character this scene has its TN reduced by 1.

science.name: Field Repair
science.flavor: Most damage in the field is mechanical, and most mechanical damage is reversible with the right tools and enough time. The "enough time" part is usually the problem.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action (requires tools), make a TN 3 Mechanics (Precision) check targeting one item at range 0.

Effects:

On a success, remove the Damaged quality from the target. If the target is Destroyed, it becomes Damaged instead. The repair holds for the remainder of the scene.
opportunities: Precision (op): Remove any quality the item gained as a result of damage or malfunction.

science.name: Grease The Joints
science.flavor: Many small things can affect the fighting ability of a T-Doll, from grit in the joints to a discharged power supply. A skilled technician can identify and address these issues on the fly, keeping their T-Dolls in fighting condition on the battlefield.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Mechanics (Precision) check targeting one T-Doll at range 0.

Effects:

On a success, the target removes fatigue equal to 3 plus your bonus successes.
opportunities: Precision (op): The next Mechanics check targeting this T-Doll this scene has its TN reduced by 1.

science.name: Group Treatment
science.flavor: When treating multiple casualties, a medic can apply their skills in a way that benefits the whole group. By triaging and administering care efficiently, they can improve the overall survivability of their team.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Medicine (Precision) check.

Effects:

On a success, choose a number of characters within range 0 (including yourself) up to your ranks in Medicine. Each chosen character removes fatigue equal to your ranks in Medicine and strife equal to your ranks in Insight.
opportunities: Precision (op): Include one additional character within range 0.

science.name: Hazard Detection
science.flavor: The wastes are filled with invisible killers. Radiation from collapsed fluid reactors, biological agents from abandoned research facilities, chemical residues from old battlefields. The ability to detect these threats before they detect you is essential for survival in contaminated zones.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Science (Fortune) check to scan for hazards.

Effects:

On a success, you detect radiation, biological agents, chemical weapons, or other environmental dangers within range 0-3.
opportunities: Fortune (op): Determine the exact nature and severity of the hazard.

science.name: Jury-Rig
science.flavor: Sometimes the correct part is two hundred kilometers away and the engagement starts in five minutes. Jury-rigging is the skill of treating those two facts as a single problem with a single solution.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene as a Support action, make a TN 3 Mechanics (Fortune) check targeting one broken, Damaged, or Destroyed item.

Effects:

On a success, the item becomes functional for the rest of the scene regardless of its damage condition. This does not remove the Damaged or Destroyed quality; at the end of the scene, the item reverts to its pre-jury-rig state.
opportunities: Fortune (op): The jury-rigged item functions as if it also had the Reinforced quality until the end of the scene.

science.name: Pain Management
science.flavor: Pain is information. Suppressing it is a calculated risk: the patient can function, but the feedback telling them when they are making things worse is gone. A medic who administers pain management accepts responsibility for what the patient can no longer feel.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Medicine (Resilience) check targeting one character at range 0 (including yourself).

Effects:

On a success, until the end of the scene, the target ignores the TN penalties from the Lightly Wounded condition. Additionally, until the start of your next turn, the target also ignores the TN penalties from the Heavily Wounded condition.
opportunities: Resilience (op)(op): Extend the Heavily Wounded benefit until the end of the scene. When the effect ends, the target gains 3 fatigue.

science.name: Reserve Power
science.flavor: An unconscious T-Doll is a sitting duck, but if you can get their systems back online even briefly, they might be able to get back in the fight before the enemy can finish them off.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 3 Mechanics (Swiftness) check targeting one Unconscious T-Doll at range 0.

Effects:

On a success, the target removes the Unconscious condition and may act normally on their next turn.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): The target also removes the Dazed condition.
Swiftness (op)(op): The target also removes 3 fatigue.

science.name: Resuscitation
science.flavor: The window to bring someone back from unconsciousness is narrow. A medic who knows how to open it, and when to stop trying, saves more lives than one who doesn't know either.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 3 Medicine (Swiftness) check targeting one Unconscious character at range 0.

Effects:

On a success, the target removes the Unconscious condition and may act normally on their next turn.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): The target also removes the Dazed condition.
Swiftness (op)(op): The target also removes 3 fatigue.

science.name: Sensor Array
science.flavor: Knowing where the threat is before it knows where you are converts a perimeter from a guessing game into a controlled situation. A well-placed sensor array does that automatically.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Mechanics (Precision) check.

Effects:

On a success, deploy a sensor array monitoring all positions within range 0–3 from where it is placed. For the rest of the scene, you are automatically alerted whenever any character enters or exits the monitored area, regardless of their Stealth or concealment.
opportunities: Precision (op): Determine one additional detail about each detected character per (op) spent this way (direction of approach, approximate count, or whether they carry weapons).
Precision (op)(op): The sensor array is concealed; detecting it requires a TN 4 Survival or Insight check.

science.name: Stop the Bleeding
science.flavor: A rapidly bleeding wound can be fatal in minutes. By applying a tourniquet, pressure bandage, or other emergency measures, you can slow or stop the bleeding and prevent a grievous injury from becoming a fatal one.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation: Activation: As a Support action, make a TN 4 Medicine (Swiftness) check targeting an injured character who is actively bleeding. Effects: On a success, you stop the bleeding, preventing the character from suffering further damage from that wound. The character still needs medical attention to properly treat the injury and recover.

science.name: Structural Analysis
science.flavor: Every structure has a point where minimal force produces maximum effect. An engineer who reads a building the way a medic reads a patient can find it.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 2 Science (Precision) check targeting one structure, barrier, door, or fortification within range 0–3.

Effects:

On a success, you identify the target's structural weaknesses. Until the end of the scene, you and any ally who has heard your assessment reduce the TN of checks to damage, breach, or demolish the target by 1.
opportunities: Precision (op): Determine whether the structure is rigged with traps or explosives.
Precision (op)(op): Identify the optimal breach point; reduce the TN by an additional 1 for the character making the breach attempt.

science.name: Emergency Repair
science.flavor: A heavily damaged T-Doll is a liability in the field. A technician who can perform emergency repairs to get them back in fighting shape can turn a liability into an asset, even if it's not a perfect fix.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 4 Mechanics (Precision) check targeting one Heavily Wounded or Incapacitated T-Doll at range 0. You must have access to repair tools to use this technique.

Effects:

On a success, remove the Heavily Wounded condition from the target. If the target was Incapacitated, remove the Incapacitated condition instead; they become Heavily Wounded. Additionally, remove any critical strike affecting the target with severity 3 or lower.
opportunities: Precision (op): Remove one additional condition (Bleeding or Dazed) from the target.
Precision (op)(op): The target also removes fatigue equal to your ranks in Mechanics.

science.name: Field Surgery
science.flavor: When a casualty's injuries are too severe for basic first aid, a medic with surgical training can perform emergency procedures in the field to stabilize them. This is a risky endeavor, but it can save lives that would otherwise be lost.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 4 Medicine (Precision) check targeting one Heavily Wounded or Incapacitated character at range 0. You must have access to medical supplies to use this technique.

Effects:

On a success, remove the Heavily Wounded condition from the target. If the target was Incapacitated, remove the Incapacitated condition instead; they become Heavily Wounded.
opportunities: Precision (op): Remove one additional condition (Bleeding or Dazed) from the target.
Precision (op)(op): The target also removes fatigue equal to your ranks in Medicine.

science.name: Forensic Analysis
science.flavor: The dead cannot speak, but their remains tell stories to those who know how to listen. A thorough examination of a crime scene or corpse can reveal the sequence of events that led to death, providing crucial intelligence about enemy operations, criminal activity, or the nature of a threat.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

Make a TN 2 Science (Precision) check to inspect a crime scene or body for forensic clues.

Effects:

On a success, you determine what happened to the victim, including cause of death and sequence of events.
opportunities: Precision (op): Determine the number of assailants involved.
Precision (op): Discover a physical trail (blood, footprints, fibers) that reveals the direction the assailant fled.

science.name: Stabilize the Dying
science.flavor: When someone is on the brink of death, the right treatment can pull them back from the edge. By applying emergency medical techniques, you can stabilize a dying person and buy them precious time to receive proper care.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, make a TN 4 Medicine (Resilience) check targeting a dying character with the dying condition.

Effects:

On a success, you stabilize the character, removing the dying condition. The character is no longer at risk of dying from their injuries, but they remain unconscious and require medical attention to recover.
opportunities: Resilience (op)(op): The character regains consciousness and can act immediately, though they are still heavily injured.

science.name: Chemical Synthesis
science.flavor: With the right knowledge and resources, you can create chemical compounds that have a variety of applications, from improvised explosives to makeshift medicines. By understanding the properties of different substances and how to combine them, you can turn raw materials into tools for survival.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity, if you have access to the necessary materials and equipment, make a Science (Precision) check to manufacture a chemical substance. The TN is determined by the GM based on the complexity of the substance being created.

Effects:

On a success, you create the desired chemical substance. The GM determines the specific properties and potential uses of the substance based on your description and the context of its creation.

science.name: Jack of All Trades
science.flavor: All skills share the same fundamental principle: the application of knowledge to achieve a desired outcome. A versatile operator can leverage their understanding of one field to enhance their performance in another, treating their proficiency in one area as a proxy for another when the situation calls for it.

science.name: Activation:
science.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene as a Support action, you may make a TN 4 Science (Fortune) check.

Effects:

On success, choose one technical skill. Until the end of the scene, when making checks using the chosen skill, treat your rating in that skill as equal to your Science rating if it would otherwise be lower.

social.name: Appreciate the Scenery
social.flavor: Sometimes the best way to deal with a tense situation is to take a step back and appreciate the world around you.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Support action check targeting another character while you are both in Dangerous, Entangling, or Obscuring terrain, you may spend (op) in the following ways:
opportunities: Resilience (op): You and your target each remove strife equal to your ranks in Arts.
Fortune (op): You and your target each add 1 bonus die to their next check made before the end of the scene.

social.name: Artisan's Appraisal
social.flavor: An artist's work is a reflection of their skills, their emotions, and their intentions. A discerning eye can read between the lines of a painting, the notes of a song, or the movements of a performance to gain insight into the creator's mindset and motivations.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make an Arts or Performance check using the Precision approach to assess an object or performance, you may spend (op) in the following ways:
opportunities: Precision (op): Choose one Approach. You learn the creator's or performer's rating in that Approach, and any one Advantage or Disadvantage they possess that relates to it (chosen by the GM).
Precision (op): You learn the creator's or performer's emotional state at the time of creation or performance, and what they most wanted from the work.

social.name: Beware the Smallest Mouse
social.flavor: Uninteresting people are often overlooked, and that can be a powerful advantage. A skilled operator can use their unassuming nature to their benefit, slipping under the radar and catching others off guard when they least expect it.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Social skill check using the Swiftness approach targeting one or more characters, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Swiftness (op)(op)+: While interacting with you, the target treats their vigilance as 1 lower per (op)(op) spent this way, and reduces the TN of their Social skill checks targeting you by 1. This effect persists until the end of the scene.

social.name: Borrowed Courage
social.flavor: The odds are what they are. What you tell people the odds are is a separate question entirely, and one with a correct answer. A commander who needs their people to hold the line for one more hour has exactly one job: give them a reason to believe the hour is worth it. Truth is optional.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity, you may make a TN 4 Performance (Precision) check targeting an army or a number of characters who can hear you up to your ranks in Insight. You may stake up to 3 Fame to reduce the TN by that amount (minimum 1) to embroider the truth.

Effects:

If you succeed, you spread a powerful rumor of your enemy's weakness, of reinforcements certain to arrive, or of some other hidden advantage. The first time each target would receive panic or Strife during the next scene, reduce the amount they receive by your ranks in Performance (minimum 0). Whether you succeed or fail, if your side loses the battle, you lose your staked Fame (your promises proved empty). There may also be narrative consequences if individuals remember what you told them.
opportunities: Precision (op): If you fail, no one can quite recall the specifics of what you said. There are no narrative social consequences for the fabrication.
Precision (op): If you succeed, add 1 bonus die to the first Scheme action check you make during the next scene.

social.name: Cadence
social.flavor: Every skilled operative develops a private language with their close partners: a word choice, a pause, a gesture that means something entirely different from what it appears to mean. To anyone not listening for it, the conversation is exactly what it sounds like.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Social skill check using the Precision approach, you may spend (op) in the following ways:
opportunities: Precision (op): Convey a secret message that alters or contradicts the outward meaning of what you are saying to one character observing you who possesses this technique.
Precision (op)(op): Convey a secret message that alters or contradicts the outward meaning of what you are saying to one character observing you who does not possess this technique.

social.name: Field Fortifications
social.flavor: Not every battlefield offers natural cover. A skilled commander knows when to make their own. With basic tools, local materials, and disciplined labor, a defensive position can be carved from even the most exposed ground.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity or a Support action during a mass battle, using adequate supplies and a suitable area, you may make a TN 3 Command (Resilience) check targeting a position you can reach.

Effects:

If you succeed, you erect a defensive structure of trenches or short barricades in the area. In a mass battle, this structure is treated as a fortification with difficulty value equal to your ranks in Crafting plus your bonus successes, which reduces attrition suffered by the cohort occupying it by 2. In a skirmish, this structure is treated as Obscuring terrain by anyone attacking those inside from outside. This structure is temporary, and degrades completely if left to the elements for more than a few days. It can be maintained with a TN 2 Crafting (Resilience) check as a downtime activity, which might need to be made more frequently in harsh weather conditions such as rain or snow.
opportunities: Resilience (op): When you perform the Reinforce action in this fortification during a mass battle, treat the TN as reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 1).

Resilience (op)(op)+: Add one of the following terrain qualities per (op)(op) spent this way to the area extending from range 1-3 around the building: Dangerous, Entangling, Obscuring, or Recessed. During a mass battle, enemies attacking a cohort in the fortification are treated as being in terrain with the added qualities.

social.name: Get Under Their Skin
social.flavor: Sometimes the best way to manipulate someone is to push them just a little bit too far. A well-placed insult, a carefully timed provocation, or a subtle hint at a hidden weakness can all be used to get under someone's skin and make them more susceptible to your influence.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When making a Social skill (Power) check targeting one or more characters, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Power (op)+: One target gains the Dazed condition per (op) spent this way.
Power (op)(op)+: One target gains the Enraged condition per (op)(op) spent this way.

social.name: Just a Joke
social.flavor: Schroedinger's Asshole (Noun): A person who, after making a statement, waits until the reaction is clear before confirming whether they were joking or not.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Social skill check using Swiftness, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Swiftness (op)+: If you lost Humanity as part of this check by saying something crass, rude, or deliberately provocative, regain 1 Humanity per (op) spent this way.

social.name: Keep Your Cool
social.flavor: Composure under pressure is not a passive quality. It is something you practice, maintain, and occasionally have to consciously rebuild in the middle of a conversation that is trying very hard to take it from you.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene as a Support action, you may spend 1 Fortune point.

Effects:

Remove Strife equal to your Fame divided by 10 (rounded down, minimum 1).

social.name: Lighten the Mood
social.flavor: Tension wears people down. A well-timed game, a clever joke, or a shared moment of levity can break that tension before it breaks the team. The right distraction at the right moment lets everyone breathe again.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Social skill check using the Swiftness approach during a game or lighthearted activity, you may spend (op) in the following ways:
opportunities: Swiftness (op)+: Choose one participant in the game or an observer. Remove 1 strife per opportunity spent from that participant.
Swiftness (op)(op)(op): Remove 1 strife from each participant and observer instead.

social.name: Marching Orders
social.flavor: An army marching on extra rations with a good rhythm moving through the rank and file will outlast one marching in silence every time. Morale is logistics.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity, you may make a TN 4 Performance (Swiftness) check targeting an army or a number of characters traveling with you up to your ranks in Command. You may expend an additional day's rations (army rations for an army, individual rations per individual) to reduce the TN by 2 (minimum 1).

Effects:

If you succeed, you and your targets cover the distance they would normally travel in that time, regardless of terrain penalties from the march.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): If your target is an army, it removes attrition up to your ranks in Medicine.
Swiftness (op): If your target is an army, it removes panic up to your ranks in Culture.
Swiftness (op)+: One individual target per (op) spent this way removes Fatigue up to your ranks in Medicine.
Swiftness (op)+: One individual target per (op) spent this way removes Strife up to your ranks in Culture.
Swiftness (op)(op)+: Choose one mundane terrain quality that would affect the targets during the march per (op)(op) spent this way. Each target ignores that terrain quality for the duration.

social.name: Operational Insight
social.flavor: Sometimes the answer to a problem isn't found in data or analysis, but in intuition and pattern recognition. A skilled operator can draw on their experience and subconscious processing to identify solutions that elude more methodical approaches.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per session, when you make a check to recall information, solve a puzzle, or understand a complex situation, you may spend (op) in the following ways:
opportunities: Fortune (op): The GM provides you with a hint or clue related to the current situation. The usefulness of this hint is proportional to your ranks in Insight.

Fortune (op)(op): You gain a flash of insight about a character in the scene. The GM reveals one of their Advantages, Disadvantages, or a technique they possess that is relevant to the current situation.

Fortune (op)+: You may ask the GM one yes-or-no question about the current situation per (op) spent this way. The GM must answer truthfully, though the answer may be cryptic or require interpretation.

social.name: Read the Room
social.flavor: A game is a controlled environment. The rules are fixed, the pieces are known, and the only variable is the person sitting across from you. A careful observer does not just watch the board.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make an Insight (Precision) check targeting one opponent in a game you are playing with them. The TN of this check is equal to the target's vigilance.

Effects:

If you succeed, choose one skill from the following: Tactics, any Combat skill, or any Social skill. You learn your target's ranks in that skill. Choose one additional skill to learn per bonus success.
opportunities: Precision (op)(op): You learn all of your target's Advantages and Disadvantages that relate to mental acuity, willpower, or social behavior (chosen by the GM).

social.name: Social Manipulation
social.flavor: Social dynamics are a delicate ecosystem. A well-placed compliment here, a subtle criticism there: you can shape conversations without anyone realizing they're being guided. The art isn't in controlling people, but in arranging the circumstances so they control themselves.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene, as a Scheme and Support action, you may make a Culture (Swiftness) or Tactics (Swiftness) check targeting two other characters who are not hostile to each other. The TN of the check is equal to the highest Vigilance among your targets.

Effects:

If you succeed, choose one target and increase the TN of their next check by 2. Decrease the TN of the other target's check by 2. This effect persists until the end of your next turn.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): Neither of your targets realizes your duplicity in hindering one to help the other.
Swiftness (op)(op): You can use this technique one additional time this scene.

social.name: Strategic Insight
social.flavor: Knowledge illuminates possibilities that others miss. By sharing expertise or framing information in the right context, an operator can sharpen their team's focus while making threats easier to spot.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per session at the start of a scene, or as a Support action, you may make a TN 2 Science (Fortune) check targeting one character.

Effects:

If you succeed, that character treats their vigilance as 2 lower (to a minimum of 1) and their focus as 2 higher. This effect persists until the end of the scene.
opportunities: Fortune (op)+: Choose one additional target per (op) spent this way.
Fortune (op): This effect persists until the end of the next scene instead.

social.name: Tactical Assessment
social.flavor: Direct criticism often creates defensiveness. A skilled operator presents observations as tactical assessments, framing weaknesses as operational parameters rather than personal failings. This allows allies to address vulnerabilities without losing face.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, you may make a TN 2 Insight (Resilience) check to appraise the weaknesses of a character.

Effects:

If you succeed, choose one of the target's known disadvantages. The target does not apply that disadvantage to their checks until the end of the scene.
opportunities: Resilience (op)+: Choose one additional disadvantage per (op) spent this way.
Resilience (op)(op): Reduce the TN of the target's next skill check using the Approach the disadvantage is attached to by 2.

social.name: War Cry
social.flavor: Sometimes the best way to fight is to rally your allies and strike fear into your enemies. A well-timed war cry can boost your team's morale, intimidate your opponents, and turn the tide of battle in your favor.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene as a Support action, you may make a TN 2 Command (Resilience) check targeting one character within earshot.

Effects:

If you succeed and your target's Strife equals or exceeds their Composure, they remove Strife until their Strife is equal to their Composure minus 1. If you succeed and your target's Fatigue equals or exceeds their Endurance, they remove Fatigue until their Fatigue is equal to their Endurance minus 1.
opportunities: Resilience (op)(op): You may use this technique one additional time this scene.
Resilience (op)(op)(op): This technique instead targets any number of qualifying characters within earshot.

social.name: Bravado
social.flavor: Playing up your own strengths can be a powerful way to manipulate how others perceive you. Whether it's a display of confidence, a show of force, or a carefully crafted persona, the right performance can make others see you in a completely different light.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a Performance or Arts (Power) check targeting any number of characters in the scene.

Effects:

If you succeed, each target perceives your Fame as 10 higher or lower than its actual value (your choice), plus or minus an additional 10 per bonus success (maximum 100, minimum 0). If you do anything that could call your Fame into question, any character may resist with a TN 4 Insight check (Precision 5, Swiftness 2) to determine your actual Fame. This effect persists until the end of the scene.
opportunities: Power (op): Choose one character in the scene. You learn whether their Fame is higher or lower than your own actual value.

social.name: Commanding Authority
social.flavor: True authority doesn't need to threaten violence. It establishes boundaries through presence alone, creating social pressure that makes aggression seem unthinkable. A commander with this presence can defuse tensions before they escalate.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per game session as an action, you may make a Command (Fortune) check targeting a number of characters up to your ranks in Command. The TN of this check is equal to the vigilance of the character with the highest Fame among your targets.

Effects:

If you succeed, your targets cannot perform Attack actions targeting you. This effect persists for one round, plus additional rounds equal to your bonus successes, or until you perform an Attack action.
opportunities: Fortune (op)+: Choose one additional target with Fame lower than your first target per (op) spent this way.
Fortune (op)(op): Your targets also cannot perform Scheme actions targeting you.

social.name: Commanding Presence
social.flavor: First impressions matter on the battlefield as much as in the boardroom. A commander who enters with authority sets the tone for every interaction that follows, commanding attention and respect from the moment they arrive.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you enter a scene, you may make a Performance (Power) check. The TN of this check is equal to the difference between the Fame of the character in the scene with the highest Fame and your Fame, to a minimum of 1.

Effects:

If you succeed, reduce the TN of Scheme and Support action checks you make by 1. This effect persists for one round, plus one additional round for every two bonus successes.
opportunities: Power (op)(op)+: When you receive a Fame award, increase the amount of Fame you gain by 1, plus 1 per additional (op)(op) spent this way.
Power (op)(op): You gain 1 bonus die on your next check made this scene.

social.name: Look Out!
social.flavor: A timely warning can prevent disaster. By alerting allies to imminent threats and suggesting optimal defensive positions, an operator can turn potential casualties into prepared defenders.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a check to resist an effect, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Resilience (op)+: One character per (op) spent this way may immediately switch to a stance of their choice.

social.name: Manners maketh the Man
social.flavor: There are contexts where violence isn't just inadvisable, it's actively improper. A character who knows the rules well enough can make attacking a protected individual cost more than it's worth.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a Command or Culture (Resilience) check targeting one character to claim protection for an individual of your choice. The TN of this check is equal to the target's vigilance.

Effects:

If you succeed, the target must lose Humanity equal to your ranks in Command plus your bonus successes, and suffer that much Strife, to perform an Attack or Scheme action targeting the chosen individual. This effect persists until the end of the scene or until the target performs an Attack or Scheme action targeting that individual.
opportunities: Resilience (op)+: Choose one additional target whose vigilance is lower than or equal to your first target's vigilance per (op) spent this way.

social.name: Negotiation Tactics
social.flavor: "Of course, there are operational expenses to consider... logistics, hazard pay, contingency funds." Every contract has room for negotiation if you know where to look and how to ask. The difference between survival and profit is often just a well-timed pause and the right phrasing.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Negotiation (Fortune) check to negotiate payment for a job, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Fortune (op)+: If you succeed, you also convince the client to pay 10% of the fee up front per (op) spent this way.

social.name: Provocative Challenge
social.flavor: A well-aimed insult can be more effective than a bullet. By targeting an enemy's pride, insecurities, or tactical sensibilities, you can force them into making mistakes they would otherwise avoid.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene as a Scheme action, you may make a Performance or Tactics (Power) check targeting one character. The TN of the check is equal to your target's vigilance.

Effects:

If you succeed during an intrigue encounter or a duel, your target receives strife equal to their Humanity divided by 10 (rounded down, minimum 1) unless they forfeit that much Humanity. If you succeed on the check during a skirmish, that character must immediately move 2 range bands toward you unless they choose to receive 3 strife, plus 1 additional strife for every 2 bonus successes. If you succeed on the check during a mass battle, that character must target your cohort with an Assault or Challenge action next turn, unless they choose to receive 3 strife, plus 1 additional strife for every 2 bonus successes. If you succeed or fail, reduce the TN of your target's next check by 1.
opportunities: Power (op)(op): You may use this technique one additional time this scene.

social.name: Um, Actually
social.flavor: Some arguments are won by rhetoric. Others are won by arriving with more data than the other person can answer. The distinction matters less than most people think.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a Science (Resilience) check (or another knowledge-based skill at the GM's discretion) targeting one character. The TN of this check is equal to your target's Focus minus their current Strife, to a minimum of 1.

Effects:

If you succeed, your target suffers the Silenced condition unless they choose to gain Strife equal to your ranks in Command plus one for every bonus success.
opportunities: (op): If you succeed, you may add one bonus die to your next Social skill check made this scene.
(op)(op)+: Choose one additional target whose Focus is lower than your original target's Focus per (op)(op) spent this way.

social.name: Bend with the Storm
social.flavor: Sometimes the best way to weather a storm is to let it pass through you. A skilled operator can use misdirection, half-truths, and carefully crafted impressions to manipulate how others perceive them, creating a false sense of security that can be exploited at the right moment.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Social skill check using the Precision approach targeting another character, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Precision (op): Choose one Advantage or Disadvantage. The target comes to believe you possess it, without you having stated it directly or expended visible effort to create that impression. The target also believes you are unaware you have revealed this about yourself. If you do anything that could call this impression into question, any character who witnesses it may resist with a TN 5 Insight check (Resilience 6, Power 3) to see through the fabrication. This effect persists until the target encounters incontrovertible evidence to the contrary or succeeds on the resistance check.

social.name: Bond of Heroes
social.flavor: Some bonds are forged in the heat of battle. The shared experience of fighting side by side can create a connection that transcends words, allowing allies to draw strength from each other even in the darkest moments.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per session as a Support action, you may make a TN 5 Performance (Fortune) check targeting each character in the scene with whom you share a meaningful bond.

Effects:

If you succeed, each target removes 5 Strife and 5 Fatigue, plus 1 additional point of each per two bonus successes.

social.name: Concession
social.flavor: The most effective concession is the one that costs you little but looks like a major victory to the other side. Give them what they think they want, and they will walk right into the position you need them in.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a TN 3 Negotiation (Precision) check targeting one character. When you use this technique, you must give up something you know the target wants: a physical object, a concession in negotiation, or 2 momentum points toward one of their social objectives.

Effects:

If you succeed, your target cannot add momentum to their social objectives for 1 round, plus 1 additional round per two bonus successes.
opportunities: (op)(op): Instead of being unable to add momentum, when your target would add momentum to one of their social objectives, those momentum points are added to one of your social objectives of your choice instead. Your target is unaware their efforts are being diverted.

social.name: Dramatic Entrance
social.flavor: Making an entrance is an art form. The right timing, the perfect line, the ideal amount of flair, all of these can combine to create a moment that captivates everyone in the room and sets the tone for the entire conversation.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a Culture (Swiftness) check targeting a number of characters up to your Swiftness approach value. The TN is equal to the Vigilance of the character with the highest Fame among your targets.

Effects:

If you succeed, you may enter or exit the conversation without social penalty. You do not lose Humanity or Fame for interrupting, suddenly departing from, or preempting another character in the conversation, regardless of the relative Fame of those involved.

social.name: Everyone Has a Price
social.flavor: No one is completely incorruptible. Everyone has something they want, and if you can offer it to them at the right price, you can get them to do things they would never do for free.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a Negotiation (Precision) check targeting another character in the scene. The TN of this check is equal to the target's Humanity divided by 10 (rounded down, minimum 1). You must offer a bribe with a value in credits equal to the target's social threat rating × 100 to attempt this check. At the GM's discretion, this does not work on mindless ELID-infected, advanced T-Dolls with locked protocols, or other entities incapable of rational self-interest.

Effects:

If you succeed and your target is a Minion NPC, they accept the bribe and leave the scene. If you succeed and your target is not a Minion NPC, they must accept the bribe unless they receive Strife equal to your ranks in Negotiation. If they accept the bribe, they must either leave the scene, stop attempting to oppose you, or seek terms with you in some sort of negotiation. At the GM's discretion, this might deescalate a more serious conflict to an intrigue.
opportunities: (op): If your target is a Minion NPC, they join your side in the conflict instead of departing.

social.name: Intimidation
social.flavor: Intimidation is not just about making threats. It's about creating an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty that can sap an opponent's will to fight. A powerful display of dominance can make even the bravest adversary think twice before crossing you.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make a TN 4 Command or Performance (Power) check targeting any number of characters in the scene.

Effects:

If you succeed, each target suffers 2 strife whenever they choose you as the target of a Social skill check. This effect persists until the end of the scene. If you fail, you suffer 4 strife.
opportunities: Power (op)(op)+: Each target suffers 1 additional strife per (op)(op) spent this way whenever they target you with a Social skill check.

social.name: Mentorship
social.flavor: Experience is the best teacher, but a skilled instructor can accelerate the learning process. By breaking down complex techniques into manageable components and providing clear feedback, a mentor can help others master skills that would otherwise take years to develop.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

During downtime, or once per session as a Support action, you may make a TN 5 Command (Resilience) check targeting one character with fewer total technique ranks than you.

Effects:

If you succeed, the target may learn one technique you know that they meet the prerequisites for. The target gains temporary access to this technique for the remainder of the session. If used during downtime, the target gains the technique permanently, reducing the experience cost to learn it by an amount equal to your ranks in Command plus your bonus successes.
opportunities: Resilience (op): The target may learn an additional technique you know.
Resilience (op)+: You may target one additional character per (op) spent this way.
Resilience (op)(op): The target reduces the experience cost to learn the technique by an additional amount equal to twice your ranks in Command.

social.name: Misdirection
social.flavor: In games of strategy and social maneuvering, the best move is often the one your opponent doesn't see coming. By controlling what information reaches your adversary, you can guide their decisions while pursuing your true objectives unseen.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per scene as a Scheme action, you may make a Deception (Swiftness) check targeting one other character. The TN of this check is equal to the target's vigilance.

Effects:

If you succeed, you hide your true goal or objective from your opponent. Any action or ability that would reveal your true intentions or objective to the target instead reveals a false, narratively appropriate goal, subject to the GM's approval. This effect persists until the end of the scene. If you succeed, during an intrigue scene, you gain 1 momentum point toward a relevant goal.
opportunities: Swiftness (op)(op)+: Choose one additional target with vigilance lower than the original target per (op)(op) spent this way.
Swiftness (op)(op)+: If you succeed, you gain 1 additional momentum point per (op)(op) spent this way.

social.name: Perception is Reality
social.flavor: Strength and weakness are not fixed qualities. They are perceptions, and perceptions can be changed with the right words, the right timing, and the right audience.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme or Support action, you may make a Culture, Command, or Performance (Swiftness) check targeting one character. The TN is equal to the target's vigilance.

Effects:

If you succeed and chose a Scheme action, choose one of the target's advantages that you know; whenever it applies, invert it (treat it as a disadvantage instead). This effect persists until the end of the scene. If you succeed and chose a Support action, choose one of the target's disadvantages you know; whenever it applies, invert it (treat it as an advantage instead). This effect persists until the end of the scene.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): Choose one additional advantage or disadvantage and apply the effect to it.
Swiftness (op)(op)+: Choose one additional target with vigilance lower than or equal to your first target's vigilance per (op)(op) spent this way.

social.name: Prepared for Anything
social.flavor: A good operator doesn't just react to problems. They anticipate them. Through careful planning, resource management, and a touch of foresight, they ensure they have the right tool for the job before the job even begins.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, you may make a TN 1 Crafting (Fortune) check.

Effects:

If you succeed, you recall preparing an item with a rarity equal to 1 plus your bonus successes on the check. Spend 1 Fortune point to instantly produce one item you could have crafted, as long as it is reasonable (you could be carrying it on your person, have it in your quarters, or had access to the resources to craft it over the past month).
opportunities: Fortune (op): Double the rarity of the target item, but the item must be perishable or have only sentimental value.

social.name: Roast
social.flavor: Sometimes the best way to get under someone's skin is to say something that hits a little too close to home.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

Once per session as a Scheme action, you may make a TN 3 Performance (Power) check targeting a number of characters up to your Power approach value.

Effects:

If you succeed, each target suffers 2 Strife and must make a TN 5 Resolve check (Precision 4, Swiftness 2). On a failure, each target suffers additional Strife equal to their shortfall. If you fail, you suffer 3 Strife.
opportunities: Power (op)(op): For each target who reaches their Composure threshold as a result of this technique, gain 5 Fame.

social.name: Show Off
social.flavor: Sometimes the best way to get what you want is to make sure everyone knows how good you are at what you do. A well-timed display of skill can earn you admiration, respect, and maybe even a little bit of envy from those around you.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

When making an Arts or Performance (Power) check, you may spend opportunity in the following way.
opportunities: Power (op)+: The next time you receive a Fame award this scene, increase the amount by 1. If there is a character with higher Fame than you in the scene, increase the amount by 1 per opportunity spent this way instead.

social.name: Slip of the Tongue
social.flavor: People rarely lie outright. They omit, redirect, and let you draw the conclusions they want you to draw. Finding the gap between what someone says and what they know takes patience and a very specific kind of attention.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action, you may make an Insight (Precision) check targeting one character. The TN of this check is equal to your target's Focus minus their current Strife, to a minimum of 1.

Effects:

If you succeed, your target slips up and admits something they were concealing from you. If your target was not concealing anything from you, you know this with certainty.
opportunities: (op)(op)+: If you succeed, your target suffers 2 Strife per (op)(op) spent this way.

social.name: Two Heads are Better than One
social.flavor: Two people with identical experience give you one perspective. Two people with different experience give you something more useful: options neither of them would have found alone.

social.name: Activation:
social.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, you may make a TN 3 Command (Swiftness) check targeting one other character in the scene.

Effects:

If you succeed, your target has your assistance on the next check they make. Additionally, your target may grant you assistance on the next check you make. Both effects persist until the end of your next turn.
opportunities: (op)(op): Choose one skill in which you have 0 ranks and your target has 1 or more ranks. When you grant assistance to another character, you count as trained in that skill. This effect persists until the end of the scene.

street.name: Clean Hands
street.flavor: Anyone can start a fight. The skill is in finishing one lethally while walking away looking like the victim. Provoke the right response, let them throw the first punch, and by the time the body is cold, every witness in the room saw an accident.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

When you make an attack check, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: (op)+: Each observer with Vigilance equal to or less than the amount of (op) you spend this way cannot attest to lethal intent. Any Supporting evidence those observers would contribute to an investigation speaks only to the act itself, not to premeditation or malice. For the purposes of any Accusation Check, the crime is treated as a lesser charge (manslaughter rather than murder, assault rather than attempted homicide) unless other evidence of intent exists.

street.name: Field Recon
street.flavor: Knowledge of the terrain is a force multiplier. A scout who can quickly assess the environment and identify advantageous positions can turn the landscape into an ally, finding cover, chokepoints, and escape routes that others might miss.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity, or once per scene as a Movement and Support action, you may make a TN 3 Survival (Swiftness) check to survey the terrain around you. In urban environments, you may substitute Subterfuge for Survival.

Effects:

If you succeed, you learn all terrain qualities of the surrounding area (several miles in all directions if used as a downtime activity, or the full extent of the current scene's area if used in a scene), as well as the location of any fortifications within that range. While conducting this survey, you remain concealed from any character whose vigilance is lower than your ranks in Survival plus your bonus successes.
opportunities: (op)(op) (Downtime or Mass Battle): Choose one area or battle zone within range of your survey. That area gains one of the following terrain qualities of your choice: Dangerous, Entangling, or Obscuring.

(op)(op) (Other Scene): Choose a position within the area you scouted. All terrain within 3 range bands of that position gains one of the following terrain qualities of your choice: Dangerous, Entangling, or Obscuring.
(op)+: You identify the precise location and composition of enemy forces in the area whose commanders have vigilance lower than your ranks in Survival plus (op) spent this way.

(op)(op)(op) (Mass Battle): On your next turn, if you target an enemy unit occupying a fortification, that unit does not benefit from the fortification's defensive properties against your action, and you may resolve your effects as if you were inside the fortification.

street.name: Friends in Low Places
street.flavor: In the shadows of the city, information is currency. A well-connected operator can tap into a network of informants, spies, and contacts to gain insights that others can't access. The right piece of information at the right time can be more valuable than any weapon.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

Once per game session, during a narrative scene or as a downtime activity, you may make a TN 2 Subterfuge (Fortune) check to uncover an informant who can give you information about a subject.

Effects:

If you succeed, you reveal one informant who can give you information about a topic of your choice. If the informant's profile is required, use an appropriate NPC of the GM's choice.
opportunities: Fortune (op): If you succeed, choose one skill. The informant has a number of ranks in that skill equal to your ranks in Subterfuge and can perform checks with that skill to assist you until the end of the scene.

street.name: Improvised Hazard
street.flavor: Ideal conditions mean overwhelming force, clear sightlines, and perfect positioning. Ideal conditions are rare. A smart operative learns to use whatever is at hand: broken glass cuts feet, a kicked-over shelf forces a detour, and a cloud of dust blinds just as well as any deployment.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As a Movement and Scheme action, you may make a TN 2 Survival (Swiftness) check targeting one position at range 1–2.

Effects:

If you succeed, choose one of the following terrain qualities: Dangerous, Entangling, or Obscuring. All terrain within 1 range band of the targeted position gains that terrain quality. This effect persists for one round, plus one additional round for every two bonus successes.
opportunities: (op)(op): Choose one additional terrain quality (Dangerous, Entangling, or Obscuring) to apply to the terrain.

street.name: Phantom Step
street.flavor: Agility helps. So does choosing the right moment to move: the instant a guard looks away, the second a crowd surges, the beat when every eye is somewhere else. The best don't just move quietly. They move invisibly, and the difference is knowing when to go.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

When you perform an Initiative check or an Attack action check using the Swiftness approach, you may spend (op) as follows:
opportunities: Swiftness (op): If you are in Obscuring terrain, within a crowd, or otherwise concealed from direct line of sight, choose one character whose vigilance is equal to or lower than your ranks in Stealth. That character loses track of your position. They cannot target you with Attack or Scheme actions until they succeed on an Insight check with TN equal to your ranks in Stealth to reacquire you, or until you act in a way that reveals your position.

street.name: Poison Blade
street.flavor: A blade is a weapon in itself, but it can also be a delivery system. A poisoned blade can strike with the lethality of both the toxin and the steel, and the victim may not even realize they've been hit until it's too late.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack action, you may use one dose of a poison or drug you have on hand and make a TN 3 Blades (Precision) check targeting one character at range 0.

Effects:

If you succeed, the target is affected by the chosen substance and suffers physical damage equal to the weapon's deadliness plus your bonus successes.
opportunities: Precision (op): If you succeed,  the target suffers a critical strike with severity 2 plus 1 per (op) spent this way.
Precision (op)(op): If you succeed, the target is unaware of the substance until they suffer the first adverse effect caused by it.

street.name: Scrub
street.flavor: The difference between a crime and a rumor is documentation. Physical traces, access logs, witness memories: each can be managed or disposed of.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Subterfuge check using the Precision or Swiftness approaches to destroy, conceal, or remove incriminating material during downtime or at a scene you are currently in, you may spend opportunity in the following way.
opportunities: Precision or Swiftness (op)+: Increase the TN to detect or investigate the altered material by 1 per opportunity spent this way.

street.name: Alibi
street.flavor: In the world of espionage and covert operations, a well-constructed alibi can be the difference between a successful mission and a compromised one.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

When you make a Stealth, Subterfuge, or Deception check using the Precision or Swiftness approaches to surveil or engage in other clandestine activities during downtime, you may spend opportunity in the following way.
opportunities: Precision or Swiftness (op)+: If you succeed, you create one piece of Contrary evidence per opportunity spent this way.

street.name: Dead Air
street.flavor: Most engagements fail at the moment of contact. The sound draws attention, the attention draws response, and the responders close the window. Cut the sound and the window stays open.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack action using a readied weapon, you may make a TN 4 (Precision) check using the appropriate Combat skill for your weapon, targeting one character within the weapon's range.

Effects:

If you succeed, the target suffers physical damage equal to your weapon's base damage and gains the Silenced condition. Additionally, other characters at range 3 or greater from the target do not perceive that they have been struck for 1 round, plus 1 additional round per bonus success. Characters that are actively watching the target are not fooled by this effect.
opportunities: Precision (op)+: If you succeed, the target suffers a critical strike with severity equal to your weapon's deadliness plus 1 per (op) spent beyond the first.

street.name: Ghost Step
street.flavor: Elite operatives do not move around a building; they move through it. Walls, gaps, locked gates, and uneven debris are not obstacles to someone who treats the entire environment as a route. The best make it look effortless. They are simply somewhere else by the time anyone thinks to look.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As a Movement and Scheme action, you may make a TN 2 Conditioning (Swiftness) check.

Effects:

If you succeed, you move one range band, plus one additional range band per two bonus successes. This movement ignores the movement penalties of any terrain you pass through. You may also move along vertical surfaces or across gaps that could conceivably be crossed, at the GM's discretion.
opportunities: (op): Your movement produces no sound. You do not trigger detection checks based on sound or footfall during this movement.
Swiftness (op)(op): You may bring one willing character at range 0 with you, moving them the same distance along the same path.

street.name: Prepared Ambush
street.flavor: An ambush is not just about striking first. It's about controlling the moment of engagement, dictating the terms of the fight, and using the environment to your advantage. A well-prepared ambush can turn a dangerous encounter into a decisive victory.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity, or as a Support action in any other scene, you may make a TN 4 Conditioning (Resilience) check targeting yourself and a number of willing characters up to your ranks in Tactics who are within Dangerous, Entangling, or Obscuring terrain.

Effects:

If you succeed, all targets are concealed and cannot be detected by characters whose vigilance is equal to or lower than your ranks in Conditioning plus your bonus successes. Concealed characters cannot be targeted by Attack actions. This effect persists for each target until the end of your next turn, or until that target performs an Attack or Movement action.
opportunities: Resilience (op)+: This effect persists for one additional round per (op) spent this way.
Resilience (op)+: Reduce the TN of the first Attack action check one concealed target makes against a character in the same terrain by 1 per (op) spent this way.

street.name: Silent Strike
street.flavor: There is no such thing as a fair fight. There is only the fight you walked into and the one you set up. A disoriented target, a suppressed barrel, and a clear angle: one of these is a circumstance. All three is a decision.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack action using a readied suppressed firearm or bladed weapon, you may make a Precision check using the appropriate Combat skill for your weapon with a TN equal to your target's Vigilance, targeting one unaware or Disoriented character within the weapon's range.

Effects:

If you succeed, the target suffers physical damage equal to your weapon's base damage and a critical strike with severity equal to your weapon's deadliness.
opportunities: Precision (op)+: Increase the severity of the critical strike by 1 per (op) spent this way.
Precision (op)(op): The target gains the Silenced condition. Other characters at range 3 or greater do not perceive that the target has been struck for 1 round.

street.name: Volatile Dispersal
street.flavor: Not every weapon is built to kill outright. A well-deployed chemical payload does something more economical: it denies ground, degrades performance, and forces opponents to choose between breathing and fighting. Operators who understand chemistry understand that the most dangerous thing in a room does not always have a trigger.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack action, you may expend two doses of a single substance and make a TN 2 Science (Swiftness) check targeting each other character at range 0–2.

Effects:

If you succeed, each target suffers 3 physical damage, ignoring resistance. Each target must also make the Conditioning check for the chosen substance at the TN listed in the Poisons & Drugs rules, and suffers the substance's harmful effect on a failure. T-Dolls follow the normal immunity rules for organic substances.
opportunities: Swiftness (op): Move 1 range band.
(op)+: The area at range 0–2 of your position gains the Obscuring and Dangerous terrain qualities until the end of the scene.
(op)+: One target per (op) spent this way suffers a critical strike with severity 2.

street.name: What's Yours Is Mine
street.flavor: A skilled thief can take more than just a target's possessions. They can take their sense of security, their confidence, and even their breath. A well-timed strike can leave an opponent not just empty-handed, but vulnerable in every way.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack and Movement action using one readied weapon without the Cumbersome quality, you may make a TN 3 (Power) check using the appropriate Combat skill for your weapon, targeting one character at range 0–1.

Effects:

If you succeed, your target suffers physical damage equal to your weapon's base damage. If you succeed and your target is Dazed, you may take one item from their person; the size and accessibility of the item is subject to the GM's approval. If you attempt to take a readied weapon, the target may resist with a TN 3 Conditioning check (Swiftness 5, Resilience 2).
opportunities: Power (op): The target suffers the Dazed condition.
Power (op)+: Move 1 range band, plus 1 additional range band per (op) spent beyond the first.
Power (op)(op)+: If you succeed, you may take one additional item per (op)(op) spent this way.

street.name: Call the Wild
street.flavor: An animal companion can be more than just a pet. With the right training and bond, they can become a fierce ally in combat, capable of turning the tide of battle with their strength and ferocity.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As a Support action, you may make a Survival (Power) check targeting one friendly animal companion at range 0–2. The TN of the check is equal to the animal's vigilance.

Effects:

If you succeed, increase the damage and deadliness of the animal's weapon profiles by 1, plus 1 per two bonus successes. This effect persists until the end of the scene. The animal then gains the Enraged condition and removes all Strife.
opportunities: (op)+: You may target one additional friendly animal companion per (op) spent this way.
(op)+: The target animal removes 1 Fatigue per (op) spent this way.

street.name: Silent Assassin
street.flavor: There is a category of professional beyond deadly: the kind you only discover after the fact. No raised alarm. No struggle. Just stillness, and then a room full of bodies, each taken so cleanly that the last one never knew the first was already gone.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

When you perform a check to use a Street technique, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: (op)+: Increase the TN of the next check any one character makes to resist a critical strike you inflict by 1 per (op) spent this way. This effect persists until the end of your next turn.

street.name: Vanishing Act
street.flavor: The best way to win a fight is to avoid it entirely. A skilled operator can use the environment to disappear from sight, slipping away from danger and leaving their opponents grasping at shadows.

street.name: Activation:
street.activation:
Activation:

As a downtime activity, or once per scene as a Movement and Support action, you may make a TN 5 Survival (Swiftness) check targeting yourself and a number of characters up to your ranks in Tactics who are within Entangling or Obscuring terrain. In urban environments, you may substitute Subterfuge for Survival.

Effects:

If you succeed, all targets are concealed and cannot be detected by characters whose vigilance is equal to or lower than your ranks in Survival plus your bonus successes. Concealed characters cannot be targeted by Attack actions and cannot themselves perform Attack actions. This effect persists until the end of your next turn, or until any target performs an Attack action.
opportunities: Swiftness (op)+ (Mass Battle): If you succeed, each enemy unit with forces inside the terrain suffers a morale disruption; their commander must make a TN equal to (op) spent this way Command check or that unit suffers a penalty to its next order.
Swiftness (op)+ (Other Scene): If you succeed, each character you did not target who is within the terrain receives 1 strife per (op) spent this way.

(op)(op)(op): Even if you fail, increase the TN of Attack action checks targeting each of your targets by 2. This effect persists until any of your targets performs an Attack action or leaves the terrain.

vehicle.name: Bumper Tag
vehicle.flavor: Two tons of steel at speed is a statement. The best way to deliver it is through a rear bumper. Physics does the rest.

vehicle.name: Activation:
vehicle.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack action during a chase while at range 0 of a target vehicle, make a Piloting (Power) check. The TN equals the current scene speed.

Effects:

If you succeed, the target vehicle suffers damage equal to 3 plus your bonus successes (minus its armor value). The target driver must resist with a Piloting check (TN = your bonus successes + 2, Swiftness 1) or gain 1 stack of Losing Ground.
opportunities: Power (op): Your vehicle suffers 2 less damage from the collision.
Power (op)(op): The target driver suffers the Disoriented condition.

vehicle.name: Dirty Windshield
vehicle.flavor: A clean line of sight is a gift from your opponent. Gravel, dust, water, debris. The road is full of material that can be weaponized with a hard turn and the right application of throttle.

vehicle.name: Activation:
vehicle.activation:
Activation:

As a Scheme action during a chase, make a TN 2 Piloting (Resilience) check.

Effects:

If you succeed, the area at range 0–2 behind your vehicle gains the Obscuring terrain quality until the end of your next turn. Pursuing drivers treat you as having concealment from those positions.
opportunities: Resilience (op): The terrain persists for one additional round.
Resilience (op)(op): The terrain also becomes Dangerous terrain. Characters entering the area must make a TN 2 Survival or Piloting check each round or suffer the Dazed condition.

vehicle.name: Drive-By Directive
vehicle.flavor: The wheel in one hand, a sidearm in the other. Most people can manage one of those tasks competently. Doing both at speed requires a different kind of coordination, the kind earned by running enough pursuits to lose count.

vehicle.name: Activation:
vehicle.activation:
Activation:

As an Attack action during a chase, make a TN 3 Firearms check with one readied firearm from the driver's seat, targeting a character or vehicle within your weapon's range.

Effects:

If you succeed, resolve the attack as a standard Strike action. If you fail, you gain 1 stack of Losing Ground (divided attention costs you pace).
opportunities: (op): Ignore 1 point of the target's physical resistance from vehicle armor.
(op)(op): Move 1 range band before or after resolving the attack without spending an action.

vehicle.name: J-Turn
vehicle.flavor: Everyone expects the pursued to keep running. A J-turn exploits that assumption. You spin and face them. The drivers who were already falling behind see the move develop and round on you at their leisure. The aggressive ones eat two blocks of overshoot.

vehicle.name: Activation:
vehicle.activation:
Activation:

As a Movement action during a chase while you are being pursued, make a TN 2 Piloting (Swiftness) check.

Effects:

If you succeed, the chase inverts: Reverse your vehicle's facing. Halve the current scene speed (rounded down, minimum 1). Pursuing vehicles that are not Losing Ground gain 2 stacks of Losing Ground. Pursuing vehicles that are Losing Ground remove all stacks of Losing Ground (they have caught up).
opportunities: Swiftness (op): You may immediately Accelerate. If you do, scene speed increases from the halved value as normal.
Swiftness (op)(op): Gain 1 momentum on any objective involving escape or evasion.

vehicle.name: Lead Foot
vehicle.flavor: Most drivers flinch when the needle climbs. You lean in. The engine has more to give and your foot already knows the question.

vehicle.name: Activation:
vehicle.activation:
Activation:

When you perform the Accelerate driver action during a chase, you may spend (op) in the following way:
opportunities: Swiftness (op): The scene speed increases by 2 instead of 1.
